discovery: Discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows and the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts

nominees.name: Enrico Costa
nominees.affiliation: INAF - Istituto di Astrofisica e Planetologia Spaziali, Rome, Italy

motivation: For a quarter-century the origin of gamma-ray bursts was one of astrophysics' deepest mysteries. In 1997 Costa and Frontera used the BeppoSAX Gamma-Ray Burst Monitor and Wide Field Cameras to discover the fading X-ray afterglow of GRB 970228. Its arcminute localisation made the first optical counterpart possible. Kulkarni and collaborators then found the radio afterglow of GRB 970508 and, with Keck spectroscopy, measured the first burst redshift, proving that bursts are cosmological. Kulkarni's radio scintillation measurements also demonstrated relativistic expansion. These discoveries showed that bursts are the most luminous explosions in the universe. They linked long bursts to the deaths of massive stars and short bursts to neutron-star mergers, as confirmed with GW170817. They also created a new probe of the early universe. The work is a model of instrumental daring combined with decisive physical interpretation, and it opened the field of time-domain high-energy astrophysics.
